enriched_description: Offshore oil drilling structure, either fixed (steel jacket legs anchored to seabed) or floating (semi-submersible hull or ship-shaped). Fixed platform shows lattice steel framework (tubular members welded in X-brace pattern) rising from water, with multiple deck levels. Deck is flat steel grating surface with drilling derrick (tall tower structure, 40-60 m height) at center. Floating variant shows large column-stabilized hull with deck above waterline. Color is industrial (yellow, orange, or gray safety paint). Helipad (circular marked area) on upper deck. Cranes, pipe racks, and living quarters modules visible. Water splashes at base.

Cylindrical percussion instrument with shell (wood, metal, or acrylic) and two membrane heads (drum skin). Shell diameter 25-65 cm, depth 15-60 cm depending on type. Heads are stretched plastic (clear, coated, or textured) or animal skin, tensioned by metal hoops and tuning rods (6-12 rods around perimeter). Shell surface shows wood grain, metallic finish, or wrapped color pattern. Hardware includes lugs, tension rods, and mounting brackets. Snare drum variant shows metal snares (wire strands) across bottom head. Bass drum is large (50-65 cm) with felt beater marks on head.

Cylindrical wooden stick (length 40-43 cm, diameter 1.2-1.6 cm) for striking drums. Material is hickory, maple, or oak with smooth lacquered finish. Tip is rounded (wood, nylon, or felt) for striking surface. Taper transitions from thick grip end to thin tip end. Shoulder (transition zone) is curved or angular. Grip area may be unfinished wood or wrapped with tape. Color is natural wood (light tan to medium brown) with visible grain. Tip shape varies: round, oval, acorn, or barrel. Surface is smooth with slight texture from wood grain.

Exercise weight consisting of two spherical or hexagonal weight plates connected by short cylindrical handle (bar). Handle is knurled steel (textured grip), 10-15 cm long, 2.5-3 cm diameter. Weight plates are cast iron (black, rough texture) or rubber-coated (smooth, colored). Plate diameter varies by weight (10-25 cm). Hexagonal variant shows flat-sided plates preventing rolling. Fixed-weight dumbbells have welded or molded construction; adjustable types show removable plates with collar locks. Weight markings embossed or printed on plates. Overall length 30-40 cm.

Heavy cooking pot with thick walls (cast iron or enameled cast iron). Shape is round or oval with tight-fitting domed lid. Capacity 4-8 liters. Exterior is bare cast iron (black, rough texture) or enameled (smooth, colored: white, blue, red, orange). Lid features integral handle (loop or knob) and may have self-basting spikes on underside. Pot has two side handles (loop or tab style). Legs (3 short feet) elevate pot above fire for camp-style variants. Rim is flat for lid seal. Wall thickness 4-6 mm. Surface shows seasoning patina (bare iron) or glossy enamel finish.

Motorized air-moving device with rotating blades enclosed in protective cage. Cage is circular wire grid (metal, chrome or painted) or plastic grille, diameter 30-60 cm. Blades are 3-5 curved vanes (plastic or metal) mounted on central hub. Motor housing is cylindrical, positioned behind blades. Base is weighted pedestal (column stand) or clamp mount. Oscillation mechanism allows side-to-side rotation. Speed control dial or buttons on motor housing or base. Power cord extends from base. Color is white, black, or metallic. Blade pitch is angled for air displacement.

Stringed instrument with solid or semi-hollow body (no sound hole required). Body shape varies: Stratocaster (double-cutaway, contoured edges), Les Paul (single-cutaway, carved top), Telecaster (single-cutaway, slab body). Body is wood (alder, mahogany, maple) with glossy polyester or nitrocellulose finish in solid colors, sunburst, or natural wood grain. Neck is maple or mahogany with fretted fingerboard (rosewood or maple, 21-24 frets). Pickups (magnetic, 1-3) mounted on body. Control knobs (volume, tone) and pickup selector switch. Bridge is fixed or tremolo. Headstock has 6 tuning pegs. Cable jack on body edge.

Railway locomotive powered by electric motor, drawing current from overhead catenary wire (pantograph on roof) or third rail. Body is boxy steel construction (length 15-20 m, height 4-4.5 m). Exterior paint in railway livery (various colors). Pantograph is articulated metal arm on roof, folded or raised. Front features large windshields, headlights, and coupler mechanism. Side shows ventilation grilles, access doors, and bogie (wheel assembly) beneath. Roof equipment includes circuit breakers and insulators. Undercarriage reveals traction motors, suspension, and wheelsets. Surface is smooth painted steel with rivet or weld seams.

Large wall-mounted or freestanding furniture unit housing audio-visual equipment. Construction is wood (MDF, particleboard, or solid wood) with veneer or laminate finish. Dimensions: width 150-250 cm, height 180-240 cm, depth 40-60 cm. Configuration includes central TV compartment (open shelf or cabinet with doors), flanked by shelving towers, speaker compartments, and storage cabinets. Doors may be glass-fronted (revealing equipment) or solid. Cable management cutouts on back panels. Finish is dark wood (espresso, cherry), light (oak, maple), or painted white/black. Hardware includes hinges, handles, and adjustable shelf pins.

Flat rectangular paper container (various sizes: #10 business 24x10 cm, A4 22x32 cm, square 15x15 cm). Material is paper (white, brown kraft, or colored) with smooth or textured surface. Closure is adhesive flap (gummed, peel-and-seal, or string-and-button). Front face shows printed address area, return address corner, and postage stamp area (upper right). Window envelope variant has transparent plastic panel revealing inserted document. Seams are glued along edges, forming V-shaped or pointed flap folds. Thickness is minimal (0.1-0.2 mm). Surface may show postal markings, barcodes, or printed graphics.
